edges.label: H rows from the same code

notes: One deterministic ledger kernel is used three ways: forward on 10,000–50,000 paths it is the policy simulator P; linearized on a scenario tree it is the here-and-now program H; on the canonical stress s*(θ*) it gives T4′ survival and the CFP readiness stage (§3.1; §12 ADR-02).
Consistency contract: on an unreduced fixture tree H's rows reproduce the simulator's cash path to 1e-9 for fixed actions; conservation to 1e-10; intra-ADIC netting = 0 (§5.13).

Agents never touch the kernel: typed specs go to an out-of-process evaluator that prices, counts and gates them; engine packages (L0–L7) never import lab, agents, claims or idm; L10 asks the evidence compiler, never an engine (§3.1; §3.2; §2.4 TB2).

Phase I-a (seconds) solves explicit elastic LPs per tier on the linearized t₀ block (𝒯₁ T1, T3; 𝒯₂ T4′; 𝒯₃ T2 hard, T8) over reversible levers only, with PE, Secondaries and Co-investment sales excluded; Phase I-b runs the CVaR rows (𝒯₄: T6, Tier-1B) only when a screen fails (§5.5).

Recovery modes: NORMAL if u* = 0 and d₀ = 0 (CIO + CRO); EXECUTION_RECOVERY if u* = 0 but d₀ > 0, glide path g_t = d₀(1 − t/T_rec)⁺ with T_rec = 4 quarters and group delivery shares (Board item); STRUCTURAL_RECOVERY if u* > 0 on a hard row or a T6 capacity breach (Board, and owner where the band is involved) (§5.5).

In both recovery modes every card, envelope and FTP point records priced_on: restored_problem and the recovery hash; Phase-I duals appear only as infeasibility prices on the Treasurer panel (§5.5; §6.1).

Consent scenarios R0x (group levers) ⊂ R0 (+ Treasury top-up) ⊂ R1 (+ signed revolver) ⊂ R2 (+ owner band, Mode H): λ, FTP, envelopes and cards are priced on the highest scenario whose levers are signed; cards that flip between scenarios are labelled consent-sensitive (§5.5).

Pinned-dual CI test: test_no_pinned_duals (8/8) and test_no_pinned_duals_groups (18/18), extended with μ_n − M_n > 0 at every pricing node and invariance to ×10 penalties; it gates baseline pricing at T−20, and Gate 1 fails any element priced on a pinned dual (§5.6; §10.7; §3.6; §7.6).
Why it matters: a pinned dual of 100 prices every fund as a SELL at a 0.9% reservation price; after Phase-I restoration the dual is 0.237 and the price 76.8% [I-calc, SYNTHETIC] (§5.5; §4.8).

λ from KKT: ℓ_n = M_n/(μ_n − M_n); kernel π_n; FTP(h); KKT cap at the cheapest spare lever; every price carries one-sided intervals ('at a kink'), RHS-ranging validity and bands across 5 SAA replications (§5.6).

Selection: exact column pricing on CRN, then a Level-B MILP over ≤ 30 coupling rows, then fix and re-solve (≤ 5 iterations); Farley certificate Γ ≤ 5bp CE, else 'selection not certified'; forced re-solves; H–P ranking test Kendall τ ≥ 0.8 (§5.7).
Every proposal (optimizer, agent package or IC amendment) passes through module F; in recovery F projects onto the restored set including the glide path (§5.8).

MPC loop: freeze (G2) → Phase I and mode (G0) → H on 5 replications → selection, Γ, forced re-solves → module F → P certification of C_H → sealed run → IC; between quarters only IC-approved delegated rules executed by named humans (§5.9).
Probabilities are certified in P, never optimized: one-sided 95% Clopper–Pearson bounds on fresh 50k paths per final world plus B2; P(10%) is reported beside P(red) (§5.10; §5.2).
Readiness-Red is not event-Red: the planning stage = max(readiness, event) drives the pacing corridor; the event stage alone drives irreversible playbooks (§4.9; §12 ADR-08).
FBE-R reads SELL flags and envelope status from the previous quarter's frozen outputs, so the pipeline stays acyclic and G2 hashes them (§4.7).

Real Assets (added 18 Oct; research in progress; interim rules, brief §8): closed-end funds reuse the PE-fund engine with real-asset parameters and earlier income; core, open-end and direct assets use income yield plus an appraisal-smoothed (Geltner) NAV driven by cap or discount rates; capex and development calls (brief §8 rule 2).

Real Assets interim engine also carries asset-level non-recourse debt (LTV, DSCR, maturity wall, refinancing risk, rate hedges) and an open-end redemption-queue state machine analogous to the HF liquidity-terms machine (brief §8 rule 2).

Real Assets interim actions: SELL (asset or stake sale; LP-interest secondary; open-end redemption via the queue), HOLD, REFINANCE cash-out (asset-debt refi, recap, sale-leaseback or ground lease, JV sell-down, NAV facility), LEVER (acquisition or development debt) (brief §8 rule 3).

Real Assets marks: underwritten (yield-on-cost, IRR, exit cap rate); current (appraisal NAV, lagged and smoothed); forecast (business plans); market-implied (listed REIT and infrastructure NAV discounts, secondary pricing) (brief §8 rule 4).

Oil wrong-way risk: when oil is weak the owner's draw rises (fiscal state, §4.3) and Real Assets energy and natural-resource assets fall; Gulf real estate may move with the fiscal cycle; real-estate and infrastructure income pass inflation through only partially (brief §8 rule 5).
Attribution, envelopes and FTP charges are generic over groups (brief §8 rule 1); §4.13 names nine Shapley players for the seven groups plus TPA and CF.
SYNTHETIC – NOT ADIC DATA: every balance, probability, price and timing quoted comes from the synthetic working book, research prototypes or benchmark proxies (ARCHITECTURE.md header).

nodes.sublabel: forecasts can't buy budget; no ratchet; heads recuse

notes: Groups are the organizational unit and the total portfolio the decision unit: groups are price-takers inside quantity envelopes, and prices and envelopes come from the same restored optimizer (§6).

Decision prices (undamped restored duals, no floor; c_buf = 1.5% is a ceiling, never a floor) drive cards, Level-B selection and envelope requests; the published FTP (EWMA, 2-quarter half-life, ±50% collar) drives vintage-locked performance charges, and CF holds the repricing mismatch DVA_CF (§6.1).

FTP is solved nightly at Tier-1 tolerance (the default pricing level) and at appetite ('the cost of moving to appetite'); the TPC/IC states the level in Q4 and the Board ratifies the methodology in A3 (§6.1; §12 ADR-29).

Pricing uses the highest consent scenario whose levers are signed: R0x group levers ⊂ R0 + Treasury top-up ⊂ R1 + signed revolver ⊂ R2 + owner band (Mode H); Phase-I duals are infeasibility prices on the Treasurer panel only (§5.5; §6.1).

Requests above an envelope: releases are free; an increase on a binding row is priced at the dual only inside its RHS-ranging interval; up to +20% is Tier B (CIO + CRO), beyond is Tier A; no free band exceeds ≈$0.44bn; no ratchet; envelopes are refused from any pinned solve or reverse stress (§6.3).

In recovery, B_rec = Λ_g + φ_g,t·g_t: delivery shares come from the least-cost reversible group levers (no sales); a group behind schedule loses envelope one for one or buys it back at the dual (§6.4).

Pacing corridor keys on the planning stage: Green 0.75–1.25× plan, Amber 0.25–0.5× with a protected core sleeve (≥ 25% of plan), Red protected re-ups only; c^PACE prices forgone net α* after charges, GP access and lost co-investment flow (§6.5).

Contingent budgets (Secondaries purchases, Capital Solutions new money, credit-secondary purchases) clear the hurdle (1 + r_h)(1 + ℓ̄) − 1; gate = confirmed d̂ > 20% and Tier 1 green in any event stage but Black; tail-hedge cash is credited to the Overlay and never ring-fenced (§6.7; §12 ADR-28).

Liquidity raised means external cash only: every flow carries counterparty ∈ {external, intra_adic}; intra-ADIC flows count zero; both legs at fair value with any wedge to a centre line; approval Tier B, Tier A if ≥ 0.25% of NAV or conflicted (Q9); gate V2 checks netting on DVA ledgers (§6.8).

Desk conflict controls: the Secondaries desk registers external clearing-price distributions and never sets the reference quote on a deal it may bid for; Capital Solutions produces reserve prices, never transaction prices, with ≥ 3 RFQs; ADIC sales need ≥ 2 external bids or a ≥ 20% third-party strip, and a fairness opinion if ≥ $250m or conflicted (§6.6).

Overlay services: the client group bears exposure and liquidity, the Overlay bears execution and basis, CF bears funding (contingent-liquidity charge ≈27bp a year of notional; LPC credit at FTP for cash released by P2S); the PE beta rebuild after a pacing cut is booked to TPA (§6.8).

Pay: linear in vintage-FTP DVA with ≤ 10 points for WIS forecast skill; nothing scales with budget, AUM, notional or premium; ≥ 50% deferred for the Overlay head; Gate G-E makes the pay remedy a precondition for forecast precision (§6.9; §4.7).

Decision rights: Tier A (≥ 0.25% of NAV, secondary discount > 10%, conflicted internal transfer, among others) by simple majority plus the symmetric irreversibility protocol; Tier B CIO + CRO; Tier C group or desk within mandate and envelope; Board/owner for capacity breaches, structural recovery, event-Black, payout and band proposals, A1 and A3 (§8.1).

CFP stage authorities: Green Treasurer, Amber CIO, Red IC weekly, Black Board and owner (event stage for Red/Black); recusal is enforced in software; between meetings only IC-approved delegated rules executed by named humans (§8.1; §5.9).

Real Assets (added 18 Oct; research in progress; interim rules, brief §8): real estate, infrastructure, energy and natural resources via funds, co-investments and direct assets or JVs, inside the ~60% private allocation; the group taxonomy is configuration, so envelopes, FTP charges, attribution, the forecast registry and IC seats are generic over groups, and the Real Assets head gets a shadow-IC seat (brief §8 rule 1).

Real Assets asset-level debt is non-recourse and sits outside Corporate Finance's facilities, but counts in look-through leverage and in stress through refinancing risk and covenant cures; oil wrong-way risk with the owner's draw applies to its energy and natural-resource holdings (brief §8 rules 3, 5; §4.10).
Real Assets synthetic working allocation (v2, pending the user): $18bn (≈10%) carved out of PE funds ($52bn → $34bn), ≈$4bn unfunded; SYNTHETIC (brief §8 rule 6).
